supported_profile: Already decoded byte-aligned control payload, non-swapped u8/u32/signed string length, native counted narrow conversion and raw UTF-16LE wide strings.
native_rules: Positive count serializes one byte per unit; negative count serializes two bytes per unit. Count includes the trailing terminator.
INT_MIN length is rejected. Native archive+0x38 provides a positive unit limit; a nonpositive native value does not impose that limit.
Loader overwrites the final byte/unit with NUL. It does not require the received final unit to be NUL.
Wide 0xffff is changed to NUL and invokes first-NUL shrink. Ordinary interior NULs otherwise remain in the copied string.
Normal empty narrow string serializes zero count. Forced Unicode empty serializes -1 followed by a two-byte NUL.
Wide length is counted in 16-bit units, including surrogate units, rather than Python Unicode characters.
The complete narrow conversion helper copies bytes 0..127 into wide units and replaces bytes 128..255 with the caller's 0x003f argument. Interior NUL does not end its counted loop.
qualifications: The table proves fallback field consumption when Notify did not consume the message; it does not establish concrete NotifyControlMessage semantics.
Login's identity helper delegates to another uncollected function on a separate archive branch. Its conditional length/token/string path is not used as a guessed network identity schema.
The four-byte scalar swap helper is recovered; this codec does not infer the native archive's fast-buffer invariants or expose a swapped message profile.
The conversion helpers call external diagnostics after replacing high units. Those side effects remain unknown and are not represented by this pure byte codec.
Literal test vectors are derived from native instructions, not claimed to be captured server packets.
